title: The craft behind a cup of tea
summary: The skill behind Longjing tea is part of what makes a cup worth noticing. In Hangzhou’s West Lake tea-growing area, makers developed precise hand movements for working leaves in a heated pan. The national heritage register lists West Lake Longjing green-tea making as a traditional craft. That recognition concerns a body of knowledge and practice; it does not certify every commercial tea tasting or demonstration.

sections.heading: Hands, heat and leaves
sections.text: Listed in 2008 as project Ⅷ-148, the craft includes a set of ten characteristic pan-firing hand techniques. The heritage record links the tea to the West Lake district and Longjing village. A field photograph can show the growing landscape, but cannot show whether a particular tea was handmade or where it originated. If you choose a tasting, ask about the maker, origin and total price before ordering.
